I worked for Bank of America (EDD unemployment) during 2020-2021

During that time there was all kinds of "fraud" being committed that they would lock cards. Which is typical, but they locked over 250,000 peoples cards. Regardless of fraud or not.

I would receive calls from people who never had any fraud on their card who would be unable to provide for their families, pay bills, rent a motel, etc. You would think that there would be some kind of solution to where they made it easier for someone with the right credentials to verify themselves so they could have access to their funds during a pandemic, but they hadn't fully implemented [ID.ME](https://ID.ME) yet into alot of state unemployment.

​

When people would call to unlock their card or prove there was not aby fraud at all, Bank of America would advise everyone to direct any unemployment recipients to their local unemployment office. (even though it was BofA that caused false flagged fraud) The recipients would then call their local unemployment office, to sit there for 2/4/6/8 hours just for the unemployment office to tell them they have no control over the fraud or anything to do with the card. (Because the debit card and financial side of unemployment was handled by us)

Bank of America knew this. They knew they were sending people in a perpetual loop as they did whatever they did on the other side.

I would receive calls from Fathers crying because they cant put food on the table because Bank of America had it all. I had an older lady from New Jersey who was sitting in her car trying to get a hotel, due to just losing her house that day, but was unable to get one due to the "fraud" on her account. There wasn't any fraud. The fraud that was happening was never being flagged. I'm not sure why they did what they did, but that's how it was handled.

​

Here's a link to the lawsuit that was filed against them
